properties.areaDesc: Blaine, OK; Caddo, OK; Canadian, OK; Kingfisher, OK; Washita, OK
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 14 at 4:57AM CDT until October 14 at 8:00AM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Canadian County in central Oklahoma...
Southern Kingfisher County in central Oklahoma...
Southeastern Blaine County in northwestern Oklahoma...
Northern Caddo County in southwestern Oklahoma...
Southern Washita County in western Oklahoma...

* WHEN...Until 800 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 456 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Northwestern Oklahoma City, El Reno, Kingfisher, Cordell,
Piedmont, Hinton, Geary, Okarche, Sentinel, Cashion, Binger,
Calumet, Eakly, Lookeba, Rocky, Colony, Albert, Concho, Fort Cobb
Reservoir and Alfalfa.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.areaDesc: Blaine; Washita; Caddo; Canadian
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 14 at 4:54AM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
At 454 AM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Colony, moving northeast at 35 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Hinton, Hydro, Corn, Eakly, Colony, and Bridgeport.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

NWSheadline: A strong thunderstorm will impact portions of northeastern Washita, northwestern Caddo, south central Blaine and west central Canadian Counties through 530 AM CDT

properties.areaDesc: Lea, NM
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 14 at 3:47AM MDT until October 14 at 5:30AM MDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
At 347 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Hobbs, Eunice, Jal, Eunice Airport, Monument, Nadine, Jal Airport,
Humble City, Oil Center, Lea County Regional Airport, Bennett and
Industrial Airpark.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

NWSheadline: FLASH FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 530 AM MDT EARLY THIS MORNING FOR SOUTHEASTERN LEA COUNTY

properties.areaDesc: Brewster, TX; Presidio, TX
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 14 at 4:43AM CDT until October 14 at 5:30AM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
At 443 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Alpine, Alpine-Casparis Municipal Airport and Paisano Pass.

Although the heaviest rainfall has largely shifted out of the warned
area, some roads and low-lying zones may still be experiencing
flooding. Continue to take precautions!
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.
